extracted.intended_audience: quality measure developers, CMS policymakers, hospital quality staff, clinicians and stakeholders involved in measure specification and pre-rulemaking review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and specifications used in pre-rulemaking and measure development for CMS quality reporting programs (hospital, outpatient, REH), including definitions, inclusion/exclusion rules, documentation requirements, and consensus/voting processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRMR recommendation voting and consensus threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2025, we updated the PRMR voting process such that committee members will vote to either “recommend” or “do not recommend” that a measure be added to the intended CMS program(s), thus, removing the “recommend with conditions” voting option. The threshold to reach consensus on a given measure continues to be a minimum of 75 percent agreement among members. Committee members can provide considerations for CMS to review prior to implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voting options limited to 'recommend' or 'do not recommend'; a minimum of 75% agreement required for consensus. Members may submit considerations for CMS to evaluate prior to implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reevaluation and update process for measures
rubrics_metrics.description: We conduct an annual reevaluation of measures implemented in its quality reporting and value-based purchasing programs to ensure that they remain valid and reflective of current clinical practice and coding standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of annual reevaluation, CMS may update measure cohorts, risk adjustment models, or outcomes as appropriate. Updates are informed by the most recent scientific literature, stakeholder input, empirical analyses, and assessments of coding trends that may indicate shifts in clinical practice or billing patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of sepsis definition (Sepsis-2 vs Sepsis-3)
rubrics_metrics.description: While there is no one consensus definition of sepsis, Sepsis-2 (based mainly on SIRS) is highly sensitive; Sepsis-3 (based primarily on SOFA) is highly specific and risks missing patients. Based on expert clinical and TEP input, we elected to align the measure with Sepsis-2 in order to ensure cases were not missed, but also ensured no overlap with existing condition- and procedure-specific 30-day readmission measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select surveillance/clinical definitions to balance sensitivity and specificity and to avoid overlap with existing measures; document rationale (e.g., expert input) for the chosen definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance Care Planning measure inclusion/exclusion and numerator design
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no numerator or denominator exclusions as the eCQM is intended to encourage advance care planning among all adults. The numerator is designed to account for situations where a patient does not have capacity to engage in, declines, or defers advance care planning by crediting pre-existing advance care planning documents in the EHR and advance care planning discussions with documented decisions during an inpatient encounter (including those conducted with a surrogate when the patient did not have capacity and those where the patient preferred to not name a surrogate or provide an advance care plan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not exclude patients by age or baseline health; credit pre-existing documentation and surrogate-conducted discussions; design numerator to reflect real-world clinical situations including incapacity and patient declination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation requirement for ACP discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation that an advance care planning discussion with decision occurring during the measurement period includes a discussion with the patient or the surrogate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure counts ACP discussions documented with either the patient or an identified surrogate; documentation must indicate that a discussion occurred and that a decision was made during the measurement period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated health care agent as cohort attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: The designated health care agent accounts for the presence of a documented health care proxy or medical power of attorney that is either already established or identified and documented during the inpatient encounter. States vary in the hierarchy of advance care planning decision-making by an undesignated proxy, and these state specifics are out of scope for the measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat presence of a documented proxy/POA as evidence of a designated agent; do not attempt to encode state-specific proxy hierarchies within the measure specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology equivalence for POLST/MOLST forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Some state organizations may refer to a MOLST or POLST form by other terms such as: medical orders for scope of treatment (MOST), physician orders for scope of treatment (POST), clinical orders for life-sustaining treatment (COLST), or a transportable physician orders for patient preferences (TPOPP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize variant state terminology when defining acceptable documentation and value sets; include synonym forms/terms in value sets to capture equivalent documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: VHA beneficiary eligibility exception for cohort inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: This requirement is not applicable to Veterans Health Administration (VHA) beneficiaries hospitalized in VHA hospitals, who are eligible for inclusion in the cohort regardless of their Medicare enrollment status. VHA beneficiaries hospitalized in non-VHA hospitals must be concurrently enrolled in Medicare Fee-For-Service Part A or Medicare Advantage at the time of the index admission to be eligible for cohort inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply special-case inclusion rules for VHA beneficiaries depending on hospital type; explicitly document enrollment requirements for non-VHA hospitals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of qualifying isolated CABG surgery
rubrics_metrics.description: A qualifying isolated CABG surgery is defined as a procedure performed without the following concomitant valve or other major cardiac, vascular, or thoracic procedures: valve procedures; atrial and/or ventricular septal defects; congenital anomalies; other open cardiac procedures; heart transplants; aorta or other non-cardiac arterial bypass procedures; head, neck, intracranial vascular procedures; or other chest and thoracic procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude listed concomitant procedures when identifying isolated CABG cohort; use procedure code lists/value sets to operationalize exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: ED observation stay definition
rubrics_metrics.description: ED observations stays are defined as an observation encounter where the patient remains physically in an area under control of the ED and under the care of an ED clinician inclusive of observation in a hospital bed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this operational definition to classify observation encounters for measure numerator/denominator; ensure facility-level differences in observation workflows are considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strata inclusion based on principal diagnosis and mental health definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The principal diagnosis (first listed diagnosis at ED discharge) will be used to define strata inclusion. For this measure's purpose, mental health diagnoses do not include substance use disorder diagnoses. Mental health refers to mental health diagnoses, life stressors and crises, and stress-related physical symptoms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use first-listed diagnosis at discharge to assign strata; explicitly define which ICD-coded conditions count as 'mental health' and exclude substance use disorders where specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of value set data dictionary and eCQM package for numerator codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific codes required to calculate the numerator are outlined in the value set data dictionary and eCQM package (Quality Data Model—QDM output). Please refer to the “Measure Calculation” Section for information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementers must use the published value set and eCQM package to identify numerator/denominator codes; cross-reference the Measure Calculation section for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facility-type specific measure specifications (REH vs outpatient)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notably, the specifications for several components in the REH Quality Reporting Program measure differ slightly from the Outpatient Quality Reporting specifications to reflect the fact that REHs do not have inpatient beds. The version of the measure being considered for inpatient reporting matches the Hospital Outpatient Quality Reporting specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor specifications to facility type (e.g., REH vs outpatient) and document any differences; ensure inpatient reporting versions align to hospital/outpatient specs as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability guidance for endorsement and maintenance of clinical quality measures
rubrics_metrics.description: For more details on reliability guidance, we refer readers to the Reliability Guidance for the Endorsement and Maintenance of Clinical Quality Measures Document available at: https://p4qm.org/em/resources
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the referenced Reliability Guidance document when assessing measure reliability for endorsement and maintenance decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: eCQM technical specification standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services. (2023). Electronic Clinical Quality Measures (eCQMs) Specification, Testing, Standards, Tools, and Community. Available at: https://mmshub.cms.gov/sites/default/files/eCQM-Specifications-Testing-Standards-Tools-Community.pdf
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow eCQM specification/testing/standards guidance for electronic implementation, testing, and submission; use community tools and resources cited.
